question.knowledge_point: Finding the Asymptotes of a Vertical Hyperbola by Completing the Square
question.problem: Calculate the asymptotes of the hyperbola $4{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-8y-4x-16=0.$
question.worked_solution:
To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in standard form, we need to group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{y}^{2}-{x}^{2}-8y-4x-16 & =0 \\ 4{y}^{2}-8y-{x}^{2}-4x-16 & =0 \\ 4[{y}^{2}-2y]-[{x}^{2}+4x]-16 & =0 \\ 4[(y-1)^{2}-1]-[(x+2)^{2}-4]-16 & =0 \\ 4(y-1)^{2}-4-(x+2)^{2}+4-16 & =0 \\ 4(y-1)^{2}-(x+2)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{4}-\frac{(x+2)^{2}}{16}=1\end{aligned}
$$

The asymptotes of a vertical hyperbola

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1
$$

are given by 

$$
y-k=\pm \frac{a}{b}(x-h).
$$

In our case, we have 

$$
(h,k)=(-2,1),\,a=\sqrt{4}=2,\,b=\sqrt{16}=4.
$$

Therefore, the asymptotes of the hyperbola are

$$
y-1=\pm \frac{1}{2}(x+2).
$$
